headline: OpenAI Publishes Jalapeño First Results
deck: OpenAI said Jalapeño, its inference ASIC with Broadcom, delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt and 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency than GB200 and GB300 comparison systems. The published pages describe serving workloads. Deployment inside OpenAI’s own infrastructure is planned by year-end.
body: OpenAI published Jalapeño’s first results on 25 August [E1]. The company calls the part an inference ASIC, a blank-slate design for modern LLM serving, co-developed with Broadcom [E1][E2]. The June unveil page named Broadcom as the silicon and networking partner [E2]. No training claims appear on either OpenAI page [E1][E2].

The printed ranges are 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt at peak throughput and 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency than the comparison systems [E1]. Rated package TDP is 700 watts; measured sustained power on the tested workloads was at or below 550 watts [E1]. OpenAI says it normalized results using each accelerator’s published chip power rating, citing GB200 at 1,200 watts and GB300 at 1,400 watts [E1]. Those comparisons are OpenAI’s own [E1].

The named models are GPT-OSS 120B against GB200, and DeepSeek R1 670B and Kimi K2.5 1T against GB300 [E1]. On Kimi, OpenAI printed about 1.5 times higher peak performance per watt and 3.4 times lower end-to-end latency [E1]. The tests used single-token prediction on short nominal 8k/1k turns [E1]. Foundry node, die size, yield and shipping volume are unpublished [E1][E2].

OpenAI said it plans to begin deploying Jalapeño inside its own compute infrastructure by the end of the year [E1]. Gen 2 is described as deep in development [E1]. Whether a public confirmation of non-zero production serving appears by 31 December is the next inspectable clock [E1].

evidence_box.fragment: 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt at peak throughput
OpenAI and Broadcom to co-develop Jalapeño inference chip

art.caption: Inference only. Training stays on someone else’s silicon.
